parsed.study_design: Cross-sectional mixed-methods case study using pupil surveys, facility observations, and administrator interviews
parsed.population_and_sample: 166 pupils, 3 school administrators, and WASH facilities in three public rural schools in Central Kazakhstan
parsed.exposure: School-level administrative, institutional, regulatory, operational, and maintenance arrangements affecting WASH access, including responsibility for service provision, rules governing toilet and drinking-water use, budgeting, monitoring, and implementation of national standards
parsed.outcome: Availability and accessibility of drinking water, toilets, handwashing facilities, soap, warm water, drying materials, and toilet paper; service reliability, functionality, quality, privacy, and restrictions or exclusion from use
parsed.rationale: Section 2.1 identifies an empirical mixed-methods design comprising 166 pupil questionnaires, three administrator interviews, and three facility observations. Sections 3.1–3.4 report access outcomes linked to administrative and institutional practices, including locked toilets requiring a janitor-held key, permission requirements for drinking water or toilet use, maintenance responsibilities, and inadequate provision of soap and drying materials. Table A2 further identifies responsibility for WASH provision and maintenance across school administrations and local state organizations.
